paper.title_en: Engineering photon triplets: Direct optical third-order spontaneous parametric down-conversion across photonic platforms
paper.abstract_en: Direct third-order spontaneous parametric down-conversion (TOSPDC) converts one pump photon into three lower-energy photons through a <math display="inline" id="d1e588" altimg="si30.svg"><msup><mrow><mi>χ</mi></mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup></math> interaction. It offers a route to optical photon-triplet states with higher-order correlations and non-Gaussian features. Progress is limited by weak nonlinear coupling, stringent phase and mode matching of the pump and three generated fields, optical backgrounds, and losses across three detection channels. Here we review how photonic platforms address these constraints and allow control of the joint triphoton amplitude. We distinguish direct optical TOSPDC from cascaded, stimulated, and reverse-process approaches, and examine bulk, fibre, integrated-waveguide, coupled-waveguide, resonant, and metasurface platforms. We compare published source designs, rate estimates, and spectral properties, distinguishing generated, accessible, and detected triplets and the evidence for each physical process. We also discuss how to identify a direct optical triplet signal and characterise its quantum state. Finally, we outline the main challenges and future directions for direct optical TOSPDC.
